DawaAribu . (A, TA.) (tropical:) I know not the sources (or the source ) from which he has sprung

; or his ancestry, or parentage ]: (S:) or maA yuEorafu lahu maDoribu EasalapK (tropical:) No source or origin [or parentage ], nor people, nor ancestor or father, nor nobility, pertaining to him, is know. Also, (O, K, TA,) or ↓ , with fet-h to the m and kesr to the r , (Mgh,) [thus] written like majolisN by MF, and pronounced by the vulgar maDorab , but both of these are [said to be] incorrect, (TA,) A [ tent such as is called ] qub~ap : (Mgh:) or a great [ tent of the kind called ] fusoTaAT ; (O, K, TA;) the fsTAT of a king: (TA:) pl. maDaAribu . , (S, K,) originally DaEowN , or DaEawN , (accord. to different copies of the S,) the p being a substitute [for the w ], because of the form of its pl. [and of the rel. n.]

; or, as some say, the p is a substitute for an initial w , and it is mentioned also in art. wDE ; (S;) A species of tree, (S, K, TA,) in the desert: or it is [ a plant ] like the [ species of panic grass called ] vumaAm : (TA:) accord. to Az, a species of vumaAm : (TA in art. vm :) or another plant: and some pronounce it DiEapN ; but this is in AlHasab [or grounds of pretension to respect &c.], and does not belong to the present art.: (TA:) the pl. is DaEawaAtN . (S, TA.) [Golius says, on the authority of Meyd, that it also signifies The reed of which writing-reeds are made. ]

senses.text: 1 , aor , inf. n. DagovN , He collected together the thing: whence DigovN signifying “ a handful of herbs &c. ” (Msb.) See also

2. ― -b2- And [hence,] Dagava AlHadiyva , (A, K,) aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (S,) (tropical:) He confused, or confounded, [or related in a confused manner, ] the tradition, or story, or the like. (S, A, K) ― -b3- And Dagava Alv~awoba (tropical:) He washed the garment, or piece of cloth, without cleansing it, (O, K, TA,) so that it remained in a dubious state. (TA.) -A2- Dagava Als~anaAma , aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (S,) He felt the camel's hump in order to know whether it were fat or not: (S, K:) and DagavahaA he felt her [i. e. a she-camel] for that purpose. (TA.) -A3- Dagava , accord. to the K, [and the O, as on the authority of Fr,] is also said of a waral , meaning It uttered a cry: but this is correctly with b [i. e. Dagaba ]. (TA.)

2 He made the plants, or herbage, what are termed A^aDoEaAv [pl. of DiEovN ]. (A, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Dg~v raA^osahu (assumed tropical:) He poured water upon his head, and then divided the hair with his fingers into separate handfuls, in order that the water might reach to the skin. (L, TA.) [But see what follows.] It is said in a trad. of 'Áïsheh, kaAnato tuDag~ivu raA^osahaA , (TA,) or rA^shA ↓ , (so in the JM,) meaning She used to rub about the hair of her head with her hand, in washing, as though mixing it together, in order that the water with which she washed might enter into it. (TA.)
4 , said of a dreamer, (tropical:) He related the dream confusedly. (A, TA.)
8 He collected a handful of herbage, fresh and dry mixed together. (K.)
The state of a thing's being confused, one part with another. (TA.)

A handful of herbs, (AHn, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) mixed together, (S, A, Msb, K,) fresh and dry: (S, Msb, K:) or a handful of twigs of trees or shrubs; (Mgh, * Msb;) or of fruit-stalks of the raceme of a palm-tree: (Mgh, Msb:) originally, a number of twigs all having one root or stem: and afterwards applied to what is collected together: (Msb:) or a thing that one collects together, such as a bundle of [ the species of trefoil called ] raTobap ; and of what has a stem, and grows tall: (Fr, TA:) or whatever is collected together, and grasped with the hand: (AHeyth, TA:) or a bundle of herbs mixed together

; or of firewood: pl. A^aDogaAvN . (TA.) In the Kur xxxviii. 43, it is said to mean A bundle of rushes ( A^asal , so in the Mgh and the O, in my copy of the Msb Avl [which I think a mistranscription, on account of what follows]), a hundred in number, (O, Msb,) consisting of slender stalks without leaves, (Mgh, Msb,) whereof mats are made. (Msb.) See also a prov. cited and expl. voce A_ilaAlapN .

Hence, in a trad., DigovaAni mino naArK , meaning (tropical:) Two bundles of lighted firewood. (TA.) And, in another trad., minohumu AlA=xi*u AlD~igova , meaning (assumed tropical:) Among them is he who obtains somewhat of worldly goods. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) What is confused, and without truth, or reality, [of dreams, and] of news, or tidings, and of an affair. (Sh, TA.) A^aDogaAvu A^aHolaAmK , [occurring in the Kur xii.

44 and xxi. 5,] of which the sing. is Digovu HulomK , (Msb,) means (tropical:) Complications of dreams; (A;) or medleys of dreams, falsely resembling true dreams: (O, Msb:) or a dream of which the interpretation will not prove true, because of its confusedness: (ISh, S, K:) or a false dream; the pl. form being used to give emphasis to the meaning of unreality, or because the phrase comprehends various things: (Bd in xii. 44:) or A^aDogaAvu Alr~uw^oyaA means the terrors, or frightful things, of the dream. (Mujáhid, O, TA.) One says also, A^ataAnaA biA^aDogaAvK mina AlA^axobaAri , meaning (tropical:) He brought us [ various ] sorts of news, or tidings. (TA.) DigovN means also (assumed tropical:) A deed that is of a mixed kind, not pure, or not sincere. (IAth and O, from a trad.) And kalaAmN

, applied to a she-camel, i. q. DabuwvN ; (S, K;) i. e. Of which one doubts whether she be fat, and which one therefore feels with his hand; (S;) or of which one feels the hump, in order to know whether she be fat or not: pl. DugovN . (TA.) And A camel's hump of which one doubts whether it be fat or not. (Kr, TA.)
A confused company of men. (O.)

One who hides himself in a thicket or the like, and frightens boys by a sound reiterated in his fauces: (S:) the author of the K, following Sgh in the TS and O, and Az in the T, says that this is a mistake, and that the word is correctly written with b [i. e. DaAgibN ]; but IF and IM and others write it as in the S. (TA.)
Rain that moistens the earth and the herbage. (K.)

senses.text: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. DagoTN , (S, Mgh, Msb,) He pressed him; pushed him; (S, Msb, K;) squeezed him; (Mgh, * Msb, K;) against ( A_ilaY , S, Msb, K, [and EalaY ,]) a thing, (K,) or a wall, (S, Msb,) and the like, (S,) and the ground: (TA:) he straitened him: he overcame, subdued, or overpowered, him

; or he constrained him. (TA.) It is said in a trad., latuDogaTun~a EalaY baAbi Aljan~api Ye shall assuredly be pressed, or pushed, against the gate of Paradise. (TA.) You say of a tight boot, DagaTa rijolahu [ It compressed, or pinched, his foot ]. (K in art. Hzq .) And you say also, DagaTa Ealayohi , and ↓ , (Lh, TA,) which latter, by rule, should be AiDoTagaTa , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He treated him with hardness, severity, or rigour, with respect to a debt or the like. (Lh, TA.)

3 , (K,) inf. n. DigaATN (IDrd, T, O, TA) and muDaAgaTapN ; (IDrd, O;) and ↓ ; (IDrd, O, K;) They pressed, pushed, crowded, or straitened, one another; syns. zaAHamuwA and AzdHmwA . (IDrd, O, K.) You say, Aln~aAsu ↓ fiY AlAizodiHaAmi [ The people pressed, or pushed, one another in crowding together ]; and DigaATN is like taDaAguTN . (T, TA.)

(or xxii.) 25, he pressed, or squeezed, himself, against ( A_ilaY ) a wall: and also,] (assumed tropical:) he (a man) was, or became, overcome, subdued, or overpowered
; or constrained; syn. Ainoqahara . (TA.)

The pressure of the grave; (S, Msb, K;) because it straitens the dead: (Msb:) its straitening. (Mgh.) ― -b2- It is also expl. by En-Nadr [ISh] as signifying mjAhrp [app. a mistake for mujaAhadapN , as meaning (assumed tropical:) The exertion of one's utmost power, ability, or endeavour, in contending with another: and in this sense it should perhaps be written ↓ ]. (TA.) ― -b3- See also DugoTapN , in two places.

(tropical:) Straitness; difficulty; distress; affliction; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ . (TA.) You say, Aall~`hum~a A@rofaEo Ean~aA h`*ihi AlD~ugoTapa [ O God, withdraw, put away, or remove, from us this straitness, &c.]. (S.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) Force, constraint, compulsion; (Mgh;) as also ↓ : (TA: [in which one of the syns. is written qabor , evidently a mistake for qahorN , one of the syns. of the former word in the Mgh:]) constraint, or compulsion, against the will of the object thereof. (S, * K.) You say, A^axa*otu fulaAnFA DagoTapF (assumed tropical:) I treated such a one with hardness, severity, or rigour, to constrain him, or compel him, to do the thing against his will. (S.) And hence the trad. of Shureyh, kaAna laA yujiyzu AlD~ugoTapa (assumed tropical:) He used not to allow th

A well having by the side of it another well, (As, S, O, K) and one of them becomes foul with black mud, (As, S, O,) or and one of them becomes choked up, and foul with black mud, (K,) so that its water becomes stinking, and it flows into the water of the sweet well, and corrupts it, so that no one drinks of it: (As, S, O, K:) or a well that is dug by the side of another well, in consequence of which its water becomes little in quantity: or a well dug between two wells that have become choked up. (O.) -A2- And A man weak in judgment, (K, TA,) that will not be roused to action with the people: (TA:) pl. DagoTaY , (K, TA,) [like maroDaY &c.,] because it is as though it were [significant of suffering from] a disease. (TA.)

A slitting in the arm-pit of a camel, (S, K,) and abundance of flesh [ in that part, pressing against the side ]: (S:) and i. q. Dab~N : (S, K) or a thing like a bag: (TA:) a tumour in the armpit of a camel, like a bag, straitening him: (Meyd: see muEar~akN :) or skin collected together: or the base of the callous protuberance upon the breast of a camel pressing against the place of the arm-pit, and marking, or scarring, and excoriating, it. (TA.) Accord. to IDrd, baEiyrN bihi DaAgiTN means A camel whose arm-pit comes in contact with his side so as to mark it, or scar it. (TA.) -A2- (tropical:) A watcher, keeper, or guardian; a confidential superintendent; (S, K;) over a person; so called because he straitens him; (S;) or over a thing. (K.) You say, A^rosalahu DaAgiTFA EalaY fulaAnK (tropi

; or he meant, by DAgT , the trust committed to him by God, which he had taken upon himself; but his wife imagined that there was with him a watcher who straitened him, and prevented his taking to please her. (L.)

senses.text: 1 , (AZ, S, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. (S.) [See also DigonN below.] ― -b2- And, (IAar, S, K,) aor. and inf. ns. as above, (TA,) He inclined, (IAar, S, K, TA,) A_ilayohi towards him, (IAar, TA,) and Ealayohi against him, (TA,) and A_ilaY Ald~unoyaA [ towards the present world, or worldly things ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And ADTgnhu He took it (i. e. a thing, and weapon, S) beneath his HiDon [or the part between his armpit and flank, &c.]: (S, K:) and he carried him (i. e. a child) in that part, or in his bosom. (TA.) ― -b4- AlAiDoTigaAnu is also syn. with AlAi$otimaAlu , which is The putting [ a portion of ] the garment beneath [ and within ] the right arm, [app. from behind, ] and the other end beneath the left arm, and drawing it [i. e. the garment ] together with the left hand. [said by some to be an inf. n.: (see 1:)] Rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ : (S, K:) or both signify vehement rancour &c.; and enmity; and violent hatred: (TA:) the pl. of the former is A^aDogaAnN ; (MA, Msb;) and that of ↓ the latter is DagaAy^inu , (MA,) and ↓ may be a pl. of DagiynapN , [or rather a coll. gen. n.,] or the p may be elided by poetic license

; or these two may be dial. vars., like Huq~N and Huq~apN [accord. to some], and bayaADN and bayaADapN . (TA.) One says, when he has sought to gain a person's good will, or approval, salalotu Digona fulaAnK and ↓ [ I drew forth the rancour, &c., of such a one ]. (TA.) And a woman who hates her husband is said to be *aAtu DigonK EalaY zawojihaA [ One who has a feeling of rancour, &c., against her husband ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And Difficulty of disposition in a beast: so in the phrase *aAtu DigonK [A beast ( daAb~apN ) having a difficult disposition ]. (TA.) (S.) ― -b4- And Desire

; or yearning or longing of the soul. (K, TA.) One says naAqapN *aAtu DigonK meaning A she-camel yearning towards, or longing for, her home, or accustomed place, (S, TA,) and her mates. (S. [See a verse cited voce rifaAqN .]) And sometimes DigonN is thus used, metaphorically, in relation to women. (TA.) -A2- Also A side

; or a region, quarter, or tract; syn. naAHiyapN . (K.) ― -b2- And The A_iboT [i. e. foot, bottom, or lowest part, ] of a mountain: thus correctly, as in the “ Nawádir: ” in the copies of the K, Aljamal is erroneously put for Aljabal . (TA.)
Affected with rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite; as also ↓ . (Msb.) ― -b2- And qanaApN DaginapN (tropical:) A crooked spear-shaft. (S, K, TA.) ― -b3- See also DaAginN .
A horse, and a mare, that runs like him who reverts from the state in which he was, or from the course that he was following. (AO, TA. [See also DaAginN .])
: see DigonN , in three places.
The lion: (K, TA:) as though a rel. n. from AlD~agiynapu : because he is very rancorous, malevolent, malicious, or spiteful. (TA.)
: see DaginN . ― -b2- Also A horse that will not exert his power of running unless beaten; (S, K, TA;) and so ↓ . (S, * TA. [See also DaguwnN .])
One who treats, or regards, his brother with rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite, or with enmity, being so regarded, or treated, by him; as also ↓ . (TA.)
: see what next precedes.

senses.text: 1 , aor. yaDofuw , (S, Msb,) inf. n. DafowN (S, Msb, K) and Dafuw~N , (Msb,) It (a thing, S, and a garment, S, Msb) was, or became, complete, full, ample, or without deficiency. (S, Msb, K. *) ― -b2- And It was, or became, much in quantity; (S, K, * TA;) said of property, or property consisting in cattle, (S, TA,) and of hair, and of wool. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, Dafato Ealayohi Aln~iEomapu , i. q. raf~ato [i. e. Wealth became abundantly bestowed upon him ]. (M in art. rf .) And DafaA AlEayo$u , meaning Ait~asaEa [i. e. The means of subsistence became ample ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- And DafaA AlHawoDu , (TA,) inf. n. DafowN , (K, TA,) The watering-trough overflowed (K, * TA) by reason of its fulness. (TA.) -A2- DafiYa He (a man) became poor: mentioned by Az in art. Dyq . (TA.)
A side: and DafawaAhu his, or its, two sides. (K.) [ Daf~apN and Dif~apN , also, have a similar meaning.]
[an inf. n. of 1, q. v.: and as a simple subst.,] Wealth, or prosperity, and ampleness [ of circumstances ]. (TA.) [See also what next follows.]

An easy and a plentiful state, or condition, of life. (K, TA.) One says, fulaAnN fiY DafowapK mino Eayo$ihi [ Such a one is in an easy and a plentiful state, or condition, in respect of his means of subsistence ]. (S.)

A garment that is complete, full, ample, or without deficiency. (S, Msb, K. *) And farasN DaAfiY Als~abiyb A horse full, or ample, in the sbyb [or hair of the forelock or of the mane or of the tail ]. (TA.) And rajulN DaAfiY Alr~aA^osi A man having much hair of the head. (S.) And diym~pN DaAfyapN A lasting, or continuous, or continuous and still, rain, in consequence of which the land becomes abundant with herbage. (TA.) And huwa DaAfiY AlfaDoli (tropical:) [ He is abundant in excellence ]. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, * O, Msb, * K,) third pers. Dal~a , (Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. DalaAlN and DalaAlapN ; (S, * O, * Msb;) and Dalilotu , (S, Mgh, * O, Msb, * K,) third pers. as above; (Mgh;) the former of the dial. of Nejd, and the more chaste; the latter of the dial. of the people of El-'Áliyeh, (S, Msb, TA,) and of El- Hijáz, and Kr has mentioned Dililotu for Dalilotu as heard from the tribe of Temeem; (TA;) I erred, strayed, or went astray; (Mgh, Msb;) deviated from the right way or course, or from that which was right; missed, or lost, the right way
; or lost my way; DalaAlN and DalaAlapN signifying the contr. of ra$aAdN , (S, O, TA,) and hudFY . (K, TA.) [See DalaAlN below.]
Hence, in the Kur [xxxiv. 49], qulo A_ino Dalalotu fiA_in~amaA A^aDil~u EalaY nafosiY [ Say thou, If I err, I shall err only against myself, i. e., to my own hurt]. (O, Msb. [See also x.

16 of the Kur.]) One says also, Dal~a DalaAluhu [app. His error became error indeed; a phrase similar to jad~a jid~uhu , q. v.: or his erring passed away; see 4, latter part]. (TA.) And Dal~a Eani AlqaSodi He deviated from the right way or course. (TA.) And the verb is trans. as well as intrans.: you say, Dal~a AlT~ariyqa , and Dal~a Eanohu , aor. and , (Mgh, Msb,) inf. ns. as above, meaning He erred, strayed, or went astray, from the road, or way; (Msb;) he did not find the way to the road: (Mgh, Msb:) and of anything stationary, if you miss the place thereof, you say Dalalotuhu and Dalilotuhu : (Az, Msb:) or you say, Dalilotu AlT~ariyqa , (K,) or Dalilotu Almasojida , and Ald~aAra , (ISk, S, O,) [ I missed, or lost, the right way to the road, or the mosque, and the house, ] when you know

Also, aor. (S, O, K) and , (K,) the pret. being like zal~a and mal~a , (TA,) inf. n. DalaAl , It (a thing, S, O, TA) became lost; [as though it went astray;] it perished, came to nought, or passed away. (S, O, K, TA.) Thus in the phrase Dal~a Ean~iY ka*aA Such a thing became lost from me. (Mgh.) One says to him from whom pieces of money have dropped, qado Dal~ato Eanoka [ They have become lost from thee ]. (TA.) And to him who has done a deed from which no profit has resulted, you say, qad Dal~a saEoyuka (tropical:) [ Thy labour has been lost ]: the like occurs in the Kur xviii. 104, meaning DaAEa . (TA, in two places.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) He (a man, TA) died, and became dust and bones. (K, TA.) In this sense the verb is used in the Kur xxxii. 9: but some there read, in the place of Dal

1 and 2,]) means If one of them twain [referring to women] be absent from her memory: or if the memory of one of them twain be absent from her: [or if one of them twain err in her memory: ] or, accord. to Zj, the meaning of the verb in this case is that which next follows. (TA.) ― -b6- Dalilotu Al$~aYo'a also signifies (assumed tropical:) I forgot the thing: whence one says of a woman, Dal~ato A^ay~aAma HayoDihaA (assumed tropical:) [ She forgot the days of her menstruation ]; and so ↓ : (Mgh:) or Dal~a fulaAnFA (assumed tropical:) He was made, or caused, to forget such a one. (K. [In the CK, Aunosiyohi is erroneously put for A^unosiyahu .]) It is said that laA yaDil~u rab~iY , in the Kur xx. 54, means (assumed tropical:) My Lord will not be unmindful: or nothing will escape Him. (TA.) ― -

2 , (S, MA, O, K,) inf. n. taDoliylN and taDolaAlN , (K,) He, or it, made, or caused, him to pursue a course that led to error, or deviation from the right way: (K: [see also 4:]) he, or it, led him astray; seduced him: (MA:) [or] he attributed, or imputed, to him error, or deviation from the right way. (S, MA, O.) Dul~ila saEoyuhumo , a phrase used by a poet, means Error, or deviation from the right way, was attributed to their labour; because they did not reach their goal. (Ham p.
771.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, Dal~ilo maAlaka Send forth, or set free, thy cattle to pasture, or to pasture where they please, by themselves. (O.) ― -b3- See also the next paragraph.
4 , inf. n. A_iDolaAlN , He, or it, made him, or caused him, to err, stray, or go astray; to deviate from the right way or course, or from that which was right; to miss, or lose, the right way

; or to lose his way. (Az, TA.) [See also 2, first sentence.] AlA_iDolaAlu is of two sorts: one of these is the consequence of erring, or straying; either as in the case in which one says A^aDolalotu AlbaEiyra (expl. above, see 1, former half)

; or the decreeing that one shall err, or stray, &c., because he has done so already, and this is sometimes the case when the A_iDolaAl of a man is attributed to God: the other sort is the embellishing [or commending] to a man that which is false, or wrong, or vain, in order that he may err, or stray, &c.: and God's A_iDolaAl of a man is of two sorts; one of which has been expl. above; the other is God's so constituting man that when he observes [and pursues] a certain course, or way, [of acting or the like], whether it be such as is commended or such as is discommended, he habituates himself to it, and esteems it pleasant, and keeps to it, and finds it difficult to turn from it, wherefore it is said that custom is a second nature. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b2- Also He, or it, made, or caused, h

1 and 9, which may be rendered (assumed tropical:) He will cause their works to be lost, or to be of no effect ], means, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, He will not recompense them for their good works; the phrase being similar to the saying qado Dal~a saEoyuka [expl. above]. (TA.) And A^aDal~a A@ll~`hu DalaAlaka (assumed tropical:) [ May God make thine erring to be no more, or to come to an end, ] is expl. by ISk as meaning may thine erring pass away from thee, so that thou shalt not err; and he adds that the saying mal~a malaAluka means *ahaba Eanoka Hat~aY laA tamal~a . (TA.) ― -b3- Also (tropical:) He buried, and hid, or concealed, him, or it. (K, TA.) You say, A^uDil~a Almay~itu (tropical:) The dead was buried. (S, O.) The phrase A^aDal~ato bihi A^um~uhu , meaning (tropical:) His mother burie

(S, O, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad. of Saad, A_in~iY A^axaAfu EalaY AlA^aEonaAbi AlD~ayoEupa i. e. [ Verily I fear, for the grapes, ] their [lit. the ] perishing, or becoming lost. (TA.) ― -b2- And DAE , (K, TA,) inf. n. DayaAEN and DayoEapN , (TA,) It (a thing) was left; left, or let, alone
; or neglected. (K, TA.)

Hence, DAEt AlA_ibilu , and DAE AlEiyaAlu , The camels, and the family, or household, were left untended, and unminded; and were left alone, or neglected. (TA.) -A2- DAE , aor. yaDiyEu , said of perfume, or sweet odour, i. q. DAE having for its aor. yaDuwEu . (Har p.

Hence, Day~aEuwA fulaAnFA is used by the vulgar as meaning They beheaded such a one with the sword. (TA.) ; or any habitual work or occupation of a man; (T, O, Msb, K) as the sewing of skins or boots and the like; and the twisting of ropes; and the weaving, or plaiting, of palm-leaves; and the culture of palm-trees ( Eamalu Aln~axoli ); and the pasturing of camels; and the like thereof; (T, O;) including the sowing, or tilling, of land: (TA:) or the DayoEap of the Arabs was the management, or tending, of camels and of sheep and goats: and the term includes a man's craft, or handicraft, or means of gain: (Sh, O:) and his traffic: (Sh, O, K:) one says to a man, qumo A_ilaY DayoEatika [ Arise to thy craft, &c.]: (Sh, O:) and kul~u rajulK waDayoEatahu , [ Every man should occupy himself with his proper craft, &c.] (Msb.) (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ (Ks, S, K) and ↓ and ↓ (K) Beautiful, comely, (S, A, Mgh, K,) pretty, or elegant; (S, A, K;) as some say, peculiarly in the face; (TA;) or applied to the face: (A:) or bright (Msb, TA) in the face: (Msb:) the first is expl. by Lth as signifying fair of face: fem. SabiyHapN and SubaAHapN : and the pl. of SabiyHN and SubaAHN , and of their fems. here mentioned, is SibaAHN . (L. TA.)

Beauty, comeliness, prettiness, or elegance; (S, A, K;) as some say, peculiarly in the face: (TA:) or brightness in the face: (Msb:) it is said that SabaAHap is in the face; waDaA='ap , in the skin; jamaAl , in the nose; HalaAwap , in the eye; malaAHap , in the mouth; Zarof , in the tongue; ra$aAqap , in the stature; labaAqap , in the qualities of the mind; and that the completion of beauty is in the hair. (L, TA.) [See 1, last sentence.]
: see SuboHN : and SabaAHN , in two places.

Intensely red blood: (K, TA:) from A^aSobaHu signifying one “ whose hair is overspread with redness. ” (TA.) -A2- A^asin~apN SubaAHiy~apN Wide spear-heads. (K, TA. [In the CK the latter word is without teshdeed.]) ISd says, I know not the person or thing in relation whereto they are thus called. (TA.) [See also miSobaAHN .]
: see SabiyHN .

Of a black colour inclining to redness: (K:) or having redness intermixed in his black hair: (Sh, TA:) or whose hair, or beard, has a red hue overspreading it: (Aboo-Nasr, Sh, TA:) or having hair intensely red: (TA:) it is nearly the same as A^aSohabu : (Lth, S:) and is an epithet applied to a man and to a lion: (S:) and to hair as meaning having whiteness naturally intermixed in it with redness; (K, TA;) of whatever kind it be: (TA:) fem. SaboHaA='u : (K:) and pl. SuboHN : (TA:) and hence [accord. to some] ↓ meaning “ the dawn; ” for, as Az says, the colour of the true dawn inclines a little to redness. (TA.) [

Hence, because of his colour,] AlA^aSobaHu signifies The lion. (K.) In the phrase A^usuwdN SuboHN , the epithet is added as a corroborative. (Z, TA.) ― -b2- And the fem., SaboHaA='u signifies A female conspicuous, or clear, or fair, in the jabiyn [or side of the forehead ]. (TA.)
A whip: (S, K:) and siyaATN A^aSobaHiy~apN certain whips: (AO, S, TA:) so called in relation to *uw A^aSobaHa , one of the Kings of El-Yemen, (AO, S, K, TA,) of Himyer. (TA.)
: see SuboHN , in two places. ― -b2- It is said to signify also Darkness; contr. of SuboHN , which is its primary signification: and accord. to EshShereeshee, redness of the hair. (Har p.

senses.text: 1 , aor. , (S, M, A, K,) inf. n. SaborN , (M, K,) He confined him; held him in custody; detained, retained, restrained, or withheld, him, or it; (S, M, A, K;) Eanohu from it. (M, A, K.) [Accord. to a copy of the A, ↓ signifies the same; but this may be a mistranscription. Hence,] Sabarotu nafosiY I restrained, or withheld, myself, or my soul; (S, Mgh;) EalaY ka*aA [ to endure such a thing ]. (Mgh.) 'Antarah says, mentioning a battle in which he was engaged, faSabarotu EaArifapF li*`lika Hur~apF tarosuwA A_i*aA nafosu AljabaAni taTal~aEu meaning Habasotu nafosFA SaAbirapF [i. e. And I restrained thereat a soul patient and ingenuous, that is firm when the soul of the coward yearns: the last word (for tataTal~aEu ) I have here rendered on the supposition that the poet describes the soul of th
; or I was patient of the loss, or want, of what I love, or like ]: (A:) and Eanohu ↓ [ I constrained myself to endure with patience the withholding myself, or the being debarred, from it, or him

; or I constrained myself to be patient of the loss, or want, of it, or him ]. (L, voce tajal~ada .) And ↓ [ The most excellent kind of patience is the constraint of oneself to be patient ]: a saying of 'Omar. (IAar.) And badaniY laA yaSobiru EalaY Albarodi (tropical:) [ My body will not be patient of cold, or will not endure patiently cold ]. (A.) And SaborN signifies also The being bold or daring [ in enduring, or attempting, a thing ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He made him, or it, firm, or fast

; or bound, or tied, him, or it, firmly, or fast. (TA.) [Hence,] Sabarahu EalaY Alqatoli , inf. n. as above, He confined him, namely, a man, and other than man, [ with bonds or otherwise, ] (K, TA,) alive, (TA,) and shot, or cast, at him until he died: (K, TA:) or he set him up for slaughter: (M:) and you say also, qatalahu SaborFA ; (S, M, Msb, K;) and Sabarahu ; meaning he confined him (i. e. a man) to die, until he died; and in like manner you say ↓ ; (S;) which latter signifies also he slew him in retaliation. (T in art. bwA^ .) And qutila SaborFA He (i. e. any living thing) was confined alive, and then shot at, or cast at, until he was put to death: (S:) or he (any living thing) was bound until he was put to death: (Msb:) or he (a man) was bound hand and foot, or held by another man,

Also, (S, Msb,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (Msb,) He confined him to make him swear, until he swore, or took an oath; as also ↓ : (S:) or he made him to swear a most energetic oath; (Msb;) as also Sabara yamiynahu , (A, Mgh,) which is a tropical phrase: (A:) and ↓ , (TA in art. blt ,) or EalaY yamiynK ↓ , (TA in the present art.,) he (the judge, or governor,) constrained him to swear, or take an oath. (TA.) And Subira He was confined, or held in custody, in order that he might be made to swear, or take an oath. (A.) And Halafa SaborFA He swore, or took an oath, being confined, or held in custody, (S, M,) by the judge, or governor, (M,) in order that he might be made to do so. (S, M.) And Sabara yamiynFA He swore, or took an oath: (TA in art. blt :) and he compelled one to take an oath. (Mg

2 , (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. taSobiyrN , (TA,) He urged him, or made him, to be patient, by a promise of reward: or he said to him, Be thou patient: and ↓ he made him to be patient: (Msb:) or the former, he commanded him, or enjoined him, to be patient; as also ↓ : (M, K:) and the first, he required of him that he should be patient: (Sgh, TA:) and ↓ , he attributed to him ( jaEala lahu ) patience; (M, K;) as also ↓ . (TA.) ― -b2- See also 1, second sentence. -A2- Sb~rwA TaEaAmahumo : see 1, last sentence. ― -b2- Sb~r Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. as above, He heaped up the thing. (O.) -A3- [ Sb~r also signifies He embalmed a dead body with Sabir , meaning accord. to Freytag myrrh; but for this I know not any authority: he mentions the verb as occurring in this sense in “ Hamak. Waked. ” p. 94, last line

3 , (A, MA,) inf. n. muSaAbarapN (A, K) and SibaArN , (K,) [ He vied with him in patience, or endurance; as shown in what follows: or] he acted patiently with him: (MA:) SaAbiruwA in the Kur iii. last verse means Vie ye in patience, or endurance: (Ksh, Bd, Jel: *) or in this instance, in the saying AiSobiruwA waSaAbiruwA waraAbiTuwA , the three verbs are progressive in meaning; the first meaning less than the second; and the second, less than the third: or the meaning is, [ be ye patient ] with yourselves, and [ vie ye in patience ] with your hearts in enduring trial with respect to God, and [ remain ye steadfast ] with your minds in desire for God: or [ be ye patient ] with respect to God, and [ vie ye in patience ] with God, and [ remain ye steadfast ] with God. (B, TA.) [See also
3 in art. rbT .]

(MA.) ― -b3- Sud~ira His (a horse's) breast became wetted with sweat. (S.) See

5. ― -b4- Sd~rhu , (TA,) or Sd~rhu fiY Almajolisi , (S,) (assumed tropical:) He placed him, or seated him, in the upper, or highest, part in the sitting-room, or sitting-place. (TA.) And Sud~ira He was advanced, or promoted. (A.) ― -b5- Sd~r kitaAbahu , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) (tropical:) He put to his book, or writing, a Sador , (S, K, TA,) i. e. a title, or a commencement. (TA.) And Sd~r kitaAbahu bika*aA (tropical:) [ He commenced his book, or writing, with such a thing ]. (A.) -A3- See also 5, where it is expl. as intrans., in two places.

3 signifies The returning, or going back, [app. with another, from water, &c.] (KL.) [The verb is probably trans., agreeably with general analogy, in all its senses; SAdrhu app. signifying primarily He returned, or went back, with him from water &c. ― -b2- Ibr D thinks that it signifies also (assumed tropical:) He vied, or contended, with him for precedence, or priority. ] -A2- Also (assumed tropical:) The exacting a fine or the like [app. from another: or the suing, or prosecuting, another, for a debt &c. ]. (KL.) You say, SAdrhu EalaY ka*aA mina AlmaAli (S, * K, * TA) (assumed tropical:) He desired, or sought, to obtain from him
; or he demanded of him

; or he sued, or prosecuted, him for; such a sum, or such an amount, of property. (K, * TA.) ― -b2- And SaAdarotuhu EalaY ka*a A waka*aA (assumed tropical:) I released him from my reckoning with him on such and such terms agreed upon by both. (TA in art. frq .) And Suwdira EalaY maAlK yuw^ad~iyhi (assumed tropical:) He (an agent) was released from being reckoned with ( fuwriqa ) on the condition of his paying certain property for which he became responsible: a phrase of the registrars of accounts. (TA in the present art.)

4 , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) and ↓ , (M, K,) and ↓ , (K,) He caused him to return; sent him, or brought him, back, (S, M, A, Msb, K,) or away; (Msb;) from ( Eano ) water, and a country [or place], (S,) and (assumed tropical:) any affair. 361.) ― -b2- [Hence,] A^aworada waA^aSodara (tropical:) He began and completed. (TA.) You say, A_i*aA A^aworada A^amorFA A^aSodarahu (tropical:) When he begins a thing, or an affair, he completes it. (A.) And fulaAnN yuwridu walaA yuSodiru (tropical:) Such a one begins and does not complete. (A.) ― -b3- And ASdr Alqawola (assumed tropical:) [ He issued forth the saying; made it to issue, proceed, or emanate, Eanohu from him ]. (Msb. [See
1.]) [And ASdr Eanohu AlfiEola (assumed tropical:) He, or it, made the action to proceed from him. ]

5 He [a man, TA) erected his chest in sitting. (TA.) SuduwrN , (S, M, Msb,) the only pl. form. (M.) a subst. signifying Return, (S, M, Msb, K,) from ( Eano ) water, (S, M,) and a country, (S,) or a place, (Msb,) and (assumed tropical:) any affair: (Lth:) as some say, from anything. (M.)

Hence, TawaAfu AlS~adari , (K, TA, in the CK AlS~adori ,) i. e. The compassing of the Kaabeh on the occasion of the return of the pilgrims from ' Arafát. (TA.) [And hence the saying,] tarakotuhu EalaY mivoli layolapi AlS~adari I left him as in the night preceding the fourth day of the days of the sacrifice: (A:) or [ as in the night preceding the day ] when the people return from their pilgrimage; (S;) meaning, (assumed tropical:) possessing nothing. (M.) -A2- Also quasi-pl. n. of SaAdirN , q. v. (M, K.)
The Sador [or breast ] (M, K) of a man [or beast]: (TA:) or the prominent part of the upper portion thereof. (T, S, M, K.) ― -b2-

Hence, (S,) A certain garment [ which covers the breast ], (S, M,) well known: (K:) a short shirt: a short diroE : and the dim., ↓ , is applied to a short shirt which is worn next the body. (TA.) A certain garment, of which the head, or upper part, is like the miqonaEap , [ covering the head, ] and the lower part of which covers the breast (M, K) and the shoulders: (M:) a woman in mourning for the death of her husband or relation used to wear a SdAr of wool: (Az:) or i. q. ↓ [q. v.] and mijowalN and A^uSodapN : (IAar:) or a certain garment with which the head and breast are covered, worn by a woman in mourning for her husband: (A:) or a small shirt worn next the body: (S:) or a diroE worn next the breast: (As:) or i. q. A_itobN [q. v.]. (T in art. Atb .) Returning [from water, &c.]; going, or turning, back, or away: (TA:) quasi-pl. n. ↓ . (M, K.) ― -b2- [Hence the saying,] maA lahu SaAdirN walaA waAridN (tropical:) He has not anything: (M, K:) or he has not a thing nor a people. : see SadorN , near the middle of the paragraph.

(TA.) -A2- AlA^aSodaraAni Two veins (M, K) that beat, or pulse, (M,) beneath the temples: (M, K:) or the two sides of a man: or the two shoulder-joints: (TA:) the word has no singular. (M.) [Hence the saying,] jaA='a yaDoribu A^aSodarayohi ; (M, Meyd, K, TA;) and some say A^asodarayohi [q. v.], (Meyd, TA,) and this is the original; (Meyd;) and some, A^azodarayohi ; (Meyd, TA;) a prov.; (M, Meyd, TA;) meaning He came beating [with his hand] his two sides, (TA,) or his two shoulderjoints: (Meyd, TA:) i. e. he came empty [ -handed ]; (M, Meyd, K, * TA;) not having accomplished the object of his desire: (Meyd:) or he came exulting, or behaving insolently,

[a subst. like ta*oriyEN and tanobiytN ] The [ fore-girth, i. e. breast-girth, or] girth that is upon the breast of the camel: (S, A: *) [the hind girth, or belly-girth,] that which is next the viyl , is called the Haqab : (S:) or the girth of the camel's saddle ( Alr~aHol ), and of the [ camel-vehicle called ] hawodaj . Hence, maSodaru A^amorK (tropical:) The way of return from, or of completing, a thing or an affair: opposed to maworiduhu .] One says, huwa yaEorifu mawaArida AlA^umuwri wamaSaAdirahaA (tropical:) [ He knows the ways of betaking himself to things or affairs, and the ways of withdrawing himself from them
; or of commencing them and of completing them ]. (A.) [See also another ex. in art. rHb , conj.

6.] ― -b3- And hence [also], the maSaAdir [pl. of maSodar ] of verbs: (S, TA:) maSodarN signifies (assumed tropical:) The root of a word, from which proceed the derivatives of verbs: (Lth, TA:) [in this sense it is a conventional term of grammar and lexicology, not belonging to the classical language; but on account of the importance of understanding its true application in lexicology, it is necessary to give here a full explanation of it: it is, agreeably with its etymology, the source (lit. place) of derivation, accord. to the grammarians of ElBasrah; and is what I term an infinitive noun: it is defined as] a noun signifying, by its original application, an accident as subsisting in, or proceeding from, an agent (as AlfaraHu [“ the being joyful ”], AlD~arobu [“ the act of beating ”], and

327.) The mSdr has the same government as its own verb: it is often, and may be at pleasure, used as an ideal subst. or abstract noun: and it is often employed in the place of an act. or a pass. part. n.: (Kull, &c.:) [when thus used as an epithet, it is employed alike as sing. and pl. and masc. and fem.:] accord. to Zj, every mSdr used as an epithet is for *uw [or *aAt &c.] followed by the mSdr , and therefore it has no dual nor pl. [nor fem.] form. (TA voce HaraDN .) [It has also other uses, which are expl. in the grammars. Used as a maSodar , it is sometimes made fem.; as it is also when used in the sense of a noun that is properly fem.: see SarofN , third sentence.] ― -b4- Aisomu maSodarK , called by some AisomN lilomaSodari , is a term applied to [(assumed tropical:) A quasi-infinitiv

327.) Some apply it also to what is [properly] termed maSodarN miymiY~N [i. e. A mSdr commencing with an augmentative m ], if not of the measure mufaAEalapN : but such is really a maSodar . (Expos. of the “ Shudhoor, ” ubi suprà.) And some of the grammarians [and of the lexicographers likewise] apply it to A noun that signifies the instrument [or means ] with [or by ] which the action signified by a mSdr is performed: as AlA^ukolu [“ food, ” as being “ that by means of which the act of eating ( AlA^akolu ) is performed ”]. (Kull, ubi suprà.) ― -b5- See also SadorN , last sentence but two.

[act. part. n. of 4, q. v. ― -b2- ] (tropical:) A man who completes things or affairs. (A.) -A2- And One of the names of the month jumaAdaY AlA^uwlaY : (M, K:) [ISd says,] I think it to be of the dial. of [the tribe of] 'Ad. (M.)
(tropical:) Those who are made to have the precedence, or priority, of the people, or party. (A, TA.)
[ , as a grammatical term, Of, or relating to, the maSodar . See the particles A^ano and kaYo &c.]

A man (M) strong in the chest; (S, M, K;) and in like manner a lion, (M, A,) and a wolf: (M:) and the lion; (S, K;) and the wolf; (K;) because they are strong in the chest. (TA.) ― -b2- See also A^aSodaru . ― -b3- A horse to whose breast the sweat has reached. (M, K.) ― -b4- A horse, and a sheep or goat, white in the upper part ( lab~ap ) of the breast: (M, K:) or (with p , A) a ewe having a black breast, (M, A, K,) the rest of her being white. (M.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A horse that outreaches others (IAar, M, A, K) with his breast: (TA:) IAar does not mention the breast. (M, TA.) [Accord. to rule, this should be muSad~irN , as is shown by a verse cited above: see

5.] ― -b6- (tropical:) An arrow thick in the part called the Sador . (M, A, K.) ― -b7- And AlmuSad~aru is a name applied to (assumed tropical:) The first of the arrows termed gufol , (M, K,) which have no notches, and to which is assigned no portion [ and no fine, in the game called Almayosir ]; these being added only to give additional weight to the collection of arrows from a dislike of suspicion [of foul play]. (Lh, M. [See Als~afiyHu and AlmaniyHu .])

A man (A &c.) having a complaint of the chest. (S, A, Mgh, Msb.) 'Obeyd-Allah Ibn- 'Abd-Allah Ibn-'Otbeh, on its being said to him, How long wilt thou utter this poetry? replied, laA bud~a lilomaSoduwri mino A^ano yasoEulaA To him who has a complaint of the chest, there is no avoiding coughing. (TA. [See also nafava .]) ― -b2- It is also often used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Grieved, afflicted, or vexed. (TA in art. nfv .)

SadoEN , (S, * Msb, K, *) He clave, split, slit, or cracked, it [i. e. a hard thing, such as a glass vessel, and a wall, and the like of these; (see SadoEN below;) or so generally]; syn. $aq~ahu ; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ , [but app. in an intensive sense, or relating to a number of objects,] inf. n. taSodiyEN : (TA:) or so as to divide it in halves: or so that it did not separate. (TA.) yawomay^i*K yaS~ad~aEuwna , in the Kur [xxx. 42], means On that day they shall become separated into two parties, a party in Paradise and a party in Hell. (Zj, O, TA.) [originally an inf. n.] A cleft, split, slit, or crack, (Lth, S, O, K, TA,) [generally] in a hard thing, (Lth, O, K, TA,) such as a glass vessel, and a wall, and the like of these: pl. SuduwEN . [properly thus termed]: (O, K, TA:) like xaloqN in the sense of maxoluwqN , &c. (O, TA.) ― -b3- And The plants of the earth; (K;) because they cleave it: (TA:) [i. e.] the plan

and ↓ , (K,) or the former only, (S,) applied to a mountain-goat, and a gazelle, and an ass, [app. a wild ass,] (S, K,) and a camel, (K,) Of a middling size, neither great nor small, but between the two: (S:) or youthful and strong: [see also SadiyEN :] or [in the CK “ and ”] the former word signifies a thing of any sort between two things; between tall and short, and youthful and advanced in age, and fat and lean, and great and small. (tropical:) [ Divisions in opinion &c.]. One says, bayonahumo SadaEaAtN fiY Alr~aA^oYi waAlhawaY (tropical:) Between them is division [ in opinion and affection

, (JK, S, M, O,) with fet-h, (S,) or ↓ like minobar , (K,) applied to a man, (JK, M,) [i. e.] applied to a courageous man, (S, O, K,) means AlHamolapi ↓ [ Earnest, not making a false show of bravery, in the charge, or assault ]; (JK, S, M, O, K;) or courageous [ in the charge, or assault ]: (JK:) maSaAdiqu , occurring in a verse of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, may be for *awuw maSaAdiqa

2 signifies The clapping with the hands; syn. taSofiyqN ; (S, K;) accord. to Er-Rághib, as being like the echo ( AlS~adaY ), inasmuch as there is no profit in it; (TA;) or it is from AlS~ad~u , because they [who practised it in their worship] used to turn away ( kaAnuwA yaSud~uwna ) from El-Islám; (K;) [see more in the second paragraph of art. In the Kur xxxviii. 1, some read SaAdi , with kesr, as an imperative from AlmuSaAdaApu (Bd, TA) as meaning AlmuEaAraDapu ; and hence AlS~adaY [i. e. the echo], because it imitates ( yuEaAriDu ) the first sound: so that the meaning is, Imitate thou ( EaAriD ) the Kur-án by thy works. (Bd.) ― -b2- [And] i. q. dab~arahu [i. e. He considered, or forecast, its issues, or results; did, performed, or executed, it with thought, or consideration

; or managed, conducted, ordered, or regulated, it ]; relating to an affair: (M:) [or] AlmuSaAdaApu signifies the turning about, or revolving, the opinion, or idea, [ that one forms ] respecting the management ( tadobiyr ) of a thing, and the doing of it: (Ham p. 35:) [or,] accord. to As, the minding a thing attentively, carefully, or solicitously: a man who had assisted his she-camel in her bringing forth said, bit~u A^uSaAdiyhaA Tuwla layoliY [ I passed all my night minding her attentively, carefully, or solicitously ]; because he disliked binding her fore shank to her arm, as it would distress her

; or leaving her, as she might go away at random and the wolf might devour her young one: and in like manner one says of the pastor, yuSaAdiY A_ibilahu [ He minds attentively, &c., his camels ]; when they thirst before the completion of their usual period of being kept from drinking, he restricts them to journeying by night so as to arrive at water on the morrow. (TA.) ― -b3- And He soothed, coaxed, wheedled, or cajoled, him
; or deceived, deluded, beguiled, circumvented, or outwitted, him

; or strove, endeavoured, or desired, to do so: syn. daAraAhu , (S, M, K, TA,) and daAjaAhu , and saAtarahu , (S, K, TA,) all of which have one meaning, (TA,) [though the last implies concealing enmity, ] and laAyanahu . A money-changer; (M, Msb, TA;) except that Sar~aAfN has an intensive signification [app. as meaning a skilful money-changer, and hence it is often used in the present day as meaning a banker ]: (Msb:) all are applied to him who knows and distinguishes the relative excellence, or superiority, of pieces of money: (Mgh:) these appellations are from AlmuSaArafapu , (S, O,) or from Alt~aSar~ufu , (M,) or from SarofN meaning “ excellence, ” or “ superiority, ” of one dirhem [or deenár] over another, (Mgh, and Msb on the authority of IF in relation to the first,) because such as excels, or is superior, is turned aside from the deficient: (Mgh:) the pl. is SayaArifapN (S, M, O, K) and SayaArifu (M) and SayaAriyfu
[and SawaArifuhaA pl. of ↓ ] The varieties, or vicissitudes, of affairs or events. (M, TA.)

A place of turning away or back: [see also munoSarafN :] hence, in the Kur [xviii. 51], walamo yajiduwA EanohaA maSorifFA , (TA,) meaning [ And they shall not find ] a place to which to turn away, or back, from it: (Bd, Jel:) or, a turning away, or back, from it: (Bd:) pl. maSaArifu . (TA.)
[pass. part. n. of 1: see its verb: ― -b2- and] see munoSarifN : -A2- see also SirofN .
i. q. mutaqal~abN [as meaning Place, or scope, or room, for free action ]. (A, voce sarobN [q. v.]; and so in the Fáïk.)

is an epithet applied to a verb [as meaning That is perfectly inflected ], opposed to jaAmidN [q. v.]. (TA, voce qado .) ― -b2- [ ZarofN mutaSar~ifN and TarofN gayoru mutaSar~ifK signify the same, respectively, as ZarofN mutamak~inN and ZarofN gayoru mutamak~inK : see art. mkn . ― -b3- wakiylN mutaSar~ifN , means A factor, an agent, or a deputy, who acts according to his own free will in the disposal, or management, of an affair. ]
is a n. of place, [meaning A place of turning away or back, like maSorifN ,] as well as an inf. n. [of 7]. (S.)

and gayoru munoSarifK denote the two different sorts of nouns, (O, K,) meaning, respectively, [like ↓ and gayoru maSoruwfK ,] Inflected, or declined, with tenween, and not so inflected or declined. (O, TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. SaromN (S, M, Msb, K) and SuromN , (M, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (M, Msb,) He cut it, syn. qaTaEahu , (S, M, Mgh, Msb,) in any manner: [i. e. it signifies also he cut it through

; or he cut it off, or severed it; for thus the meaning of qaTaEahu is generally explained:] (M:) or it signifies [only] he cut it ( qaTaEahu ) so as to separate it: (M, K:) namely, a thing, (S,) such as a rope, and a raceme of dates. (TA.) One says, Surimato A^u*unuhu i. q. Sulimato [i. e. His ear was cut off, entirely ]. (TA.) And Sarama Aln~axola , (S, M, Msb, K,) and Al$~ajara , (M, K,) and Alz~aroEa , aor. as above, inf. n. SaromN , (M,) He cut off the fruit, or produce, of the palm-trees, (S, M, Msb, * K,) and the trees, (M, K,) and the corn, or the like; (M;) as also ↓ . (S, M, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Saramahu , (S, M, MA, K,) [aor. as above,] inf. n. SaromN (S, MA,) or SuromN , (M, MA,) or the latter is a simple subst., (S,) (assumed tropical:) He cut him (i. e. another man); meaning h
2 [ He cut it; cut it through
; or cut it off, or severed it; namely, a number of things considered collectively

; or a single thing much, or in several places ]: (M:) taSoriymu AlHibaAli signifies taqoTiyEuhaA [i. e. the severing of the ropes ]: the verb being with teshdeed to denote muchness [of the action], or multiplicity [of the objects]. (S, TA.) [
Hence, taSoriymu AlA^aTobaA='i The cutting off of the teats of camels: a phrase mentioned in the TA.]

3 , (MA,) inf. n. muSaAramapN , (KL, TA,) (assumed tropical:) He effected a disunion with him: (MA:) or he cut him off from himself, being in like manner cut off by him: (KL:) or he cut him off from friendly, or loving, communion or intercourse, being so cut off by him: forsook him, or abandoned him, being forsaken, or abandoned, by him: cut him, i. e. ceased to speak to him, being in like manner cut by him: for AlmuSaAramapu signifies AlmuhaAjarapu and qaToEu AlkalaAmi . (TA.)

4 The palm-trees attained, or were near, to the time, or season, for the cutting off of their fruit. (S, M, Msb, K, TA.) ― -b2- And [hence perhaps,] ASrm said of a man, (S, K, TA,) inf. n. A_iSoraAmN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, poor, (S, K,) having a numerous family, or household: (K:) or in a evil condition, though having in him intelligence ( tamaAsuk ): [it is said that] the original meaning is he had a Siromap , i. e. portion, of property remaining to him. (TA.)
5 quasi-pass. of Sar~amahu ; (M;) i. q. tqT~E [i. e. It became cut; cut through
; or cut off, or severed; said of number of things considered collectively

; or of a single thing as meaning it became cut, &c., much, or in many places, or into many pieces ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- See also 7, in three places. -A2- Also (assumed tropical:) He affected hardiness, strength, sturdiness, and endurance, or patience
; or constrained himself to behave with hardiness, &c. (S, K.)

6 (assumed tropical:) They cut, forsook, or abandoned, one another; (MA;) they separated themselves, one from another; (KL, in which only the inf. n. is mentioned;) they severed the bond of union, or communion, that was between them; disunited, or dissociated, themselves, one from another; syn. taqaATaEuwA . (S, * MA, in the former of which only the inf. n. is mentioned.)
7 It became cut; cut through

; or cut off, or severed; (S, M, K, TA;) quasi-pass. of Saramahu ; (M, TA;) said of a rope [&c.]; and so ↓ . (M, K, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AnSrm mina Aln~aAsi [or Eani Aln~aAsi ] (assumed tropical:) He separated himself from mankind; said of the wolf and of the crow [&c.]. (ISk, S, M. *) And AnSrm All~ayolu (assumed tropical:) The night went away, or departed; as also ↓ : (Msb:) and AnSrm Al$~itaA='u (assumed tropical:) The winter ended; and ↓ Als~anapu (assumed tropical:) The year ended: (TA:) and AlqitaAlu ↓ (assumed tropical:) The fighting ended, or ceased. (Mgh.)
8 : see 1, third sentence.
Skin: [or leather: ] (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) a Pers. word (S, Msb) arabicized, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) originally jarom [correctly Jarom ]. (Mgh, Msb, TA.)

is an inf. n. like SaromN , (M, K,) or a simple subst.: (M, Msb:) [see the first paragraph, in three places: in one of its senses, there expl.,] it is syn. with hijoraAnN and qaTiyEapN : (TA:) and ↓ [likewise] signifies (assumed tropical:) Separation from a friend: pl. SuramN . (MA. [This pl. is app. there mentioned as of SariymapN ; but it is more probably of SuromN .]) -A2- Suromu Ald~iyki : see daliykN .

Tents ( A^aboyaAtN ), (S, M,) of men, (S,) collected together, (S, M,) separate from [ those of other ] men: (M:) or i. q. SirobN , (O in art. Srb ,) which means a few tents ( buyuwt [in the O, erroneously, butuwt ]) of the weak sort of the Arabs of the desert: (IAar, O, * K, TA; all in art. Srb :) and hence, (M,) a company (M, Msb, K, TA) of men, (Msb, TA,) not many

; or simply a company (TA) alighting and abiding with their camels by the side of the water: (Msb, TA:) pl. A^aSoraAmN [a pl. of pauc.] (S, M, Msb, K) and A^aSaArimu , (S,) or A^aSaAriymu , (M,) or both, (K,) but accord. to IB the latter of these two is the right, [being a pl. pl., i. e. pl. of A^aSoraAmN ,] (TA,) and SuromaAnN , (Sb, M, K,) with damm. (K.) ― -b2- And i. q. DarobN . (K. [So, app., in all the copies; accord. to the TK as meaning A sort, or species: but I think it most probable that this is a mistranscription for SirobN , with which, as has been stated above, SiromN is syn. accord. to the O.]) -A2- Also i. q. xuf~N munoEalN (M) or xuf~N munaE~alN (K) [i. e. A soled boot: that xuf~ here means a boot, not a camel's foot, is indicated by its being immediately added by SM that]

[an epithet applied to a man, but used as a subst., and therefore having for its pl. SaramaAtN ]. One says, huwa SaromapN mina AlS~aramaAti , [the last word said to be thus ( muHar~akap ) in the TA, but in the CK (in which as well as in my MS. copy of the K mn is omitted) written AlS~aromAti ,] meaning (tropical:) He is [ a person ] slow to revert from his anger. (K, TA.) -A2-
Also, [if not a mistranscription for ↓ ,] A portion of silver, melted, and cleared of its dross, and poured forth into a mould. (TA.)

A herd, or detached number, of camels, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) consisting of about thirty: (S:) or from twenty to thirty: (M, K:) or from thirty to five and forty: (M:) or to fifty, and forty; (K;) if amounting to sixty, termed SidoEap : (TA: [but see this latter word:]) or from ten to forty: (M, Msb, K:) or from ten to some number between that and twenty: (M, K:) or more than a *awod [which is at least two or three] up to thirty: (T voce A_ibilN :) or about forty: (Ham p. 753:) or less than a hajomap , which is a hundred or nearly a hundred: (Id. p. 637:) pl. SiramN . (S, * M, * Msb.) ― -b2- A portion of property. (TA.) ― -b3- And A detached portion of clouds: (S, M, Msb, K:) pl. as above. (S, M.) ― -b4- See also SariymapN . ― -b5- And see SaromapN .

and ↓ The cutting off of the fruit of palm-trees: (S, * Msb, and L voce jadaAdN :) and (L voce ja*aAdN ) the time, or season, thereof: (S, L:) or the time, or season, of the ripening of the fruit of palm-trees. (M, K.) -A2- SaraAmi : see the next paragraph, in two places.
: see SaArimN . -A2- Also The last milk [ remaining in the udder ] after what is termed Alt~agoriyz [which is variously explained (see

2 in art. grz ), in the CK and in one of my copies of the S erroneously written Alt~agoziyr ,] which a man draws when in need of it. (S, K. *) Bishr says, A^alaA A^aboligo baniY saEodK rasuwlFA wamawolaA humo faqado Hulibato SuraAmu [ Now deliver thou to Benoo-Saad a message, and to their chief, that the last milk in the udder has been drawn ]: (S:) the last two words [the latter of which is written in the CK ↓ ] are a prov., meaning (assumed tropical:) the excuse has reached its uttermost: (S, K:) thus says AO: (S:) IB says that SuraAmu in the saying of Bishr means the she-camel that is termed ↓ , that has no milk; [i.e. that the phrase means the she-camel that has now no milk has been milked; ] and that he makes it a proper name; and that he [also] means thereby the latter of the two sen
: see SaraAmN . ― -b2- Sometimes it is applied to signify Palm-trees themselves; because the fruit is cut off: so in a trad. (TA.)
: see SaArimN , in two places. ― -b2- Also a she-camel that will not come to the watering-trough to drink until it is left to her unoccupied; (K, TA;) cutting herself off from the other camels. (TA.)
i. q. ↓ , (M, Msb,) Cut; cut through

; or cut off, or severed: (S, Msb, K:) and having the fruit cut off; syn. majoduwdN ; (S, K;) applied to palm-trees ( naxol ). (M.) And the former, A heap ( kudos ) of corn or the like that has been cut, or of which the produce has been cut off; syn. ↓ . (M, TA.) And Whose ear has been cut off entirely ( Aal~a*iY Surimato A^u*unuhu ): pl. SuromN . (TA. [See also the fem., with p , voce baHiyrapN , where the pl. is said to be SurumN .]) ― -b2- [Applied to the lungs, it means properly Burst asunder. Hence the saying,] jaA='a Sariyma saHarK , [so in copies of the K, accord. the TA siHor , but correctly either saHarK or saHorK q. v., in the CK bA'a and Sariymu , which last word is obviously wrong,] meaning (tropical:) He came disappointed of attaining what he desired, or sought, and in a state

(tropical:) A man (TA) who follows his own opinion, cutting himself off from consultation with others: (M, TA:) or who acts with penetrative energy, or vigorousness and effectiveness, in the performing of his affairs: an inf. n. used as an epithet. (TA.)
What is cut off [ of the fruit ] of palmtrees. (Lh, M.)

Land ( A^aroD ) of which the seed-produce has been reaped: (S, K:) of the measure faEiylapN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlapN . (TA.) ― -b2- And A portion, (S, M, K,) or large portion, (TA,) detached from the main aggregate, of sand; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ : (M, K:) [or the latter is a coll. gen. n., being used in a pl. sense:] one says A^afoEaY SariymapK (S) or ↓ (K) [ A viper of a detached sand-heap or of detached sand-heaps ]; like as one says Hay~apu xal~K . (S in art. xl .) ― -b3- And A group, or an assemblage, (S,) or a detached number, (M,) of the trees called gaDFA , and salam , (S, M,) and A^aroTFY , and of palm-trees; and likewise ↓ , of A^aroTFY , and of samur . (M.) ― -b4- See also SariymN , in two places. -A2- Also (assumed tropical:) Decision, or determination, (S, M, K T
A detached number [or a small detached number, for it is app. dim. of SiromapN ,] of camels. (TA.)
: see SaArimN . ― -b2- Also A preparer, or seller, of Sarom , (MA,) whence it is derived, (Mgh,) i. e. skin, or leather: (MA:) or it signifies as expl. voce SiromN , last sentence. (TA.)
Cutting; cutting through

; or cutting off, or severing; and Sb says that ↓ is used in the same sense, like as Dariyb in the phrase Dariybu qidaAHK is used in the sense of DaArib . (M.) A_ino kunotumo SaArimiyna , in the Kur [lxviii. 22], means If ye be deciding, or determining, upon the cutting off of the fruit of the palm-trees. (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) A man cutting, or severing, his bond of union

; or one who cuts, or severs, that bond; and so [but in an intensive sense] ↓ and ↓ ; (M;) or this last signifies, (M, K,) as also ↓ , (K,) having strength to cut, or sever, (M, K,) the bond of his union. (M.) ― -b3-

Also, applied to a sword, (S, M, Msb, K,) and [in an intensive sense] ↓ , (M, K,) Sharp, (S, M, Msb, K,) and not bending: (M:) pl. of the former SawaArimu . (TA.) ― -b4- And the former, (S, M, K, TA,) applied to a man, (S, M, TA,) as being likened to a sword, (TA,) (tropical:) Hardy, strong, or sturdy, (S, TA,) or sharp, penetrating, or vigorous and effective, (M, K, TA,) and courageous. (S, M, K, TA.) ― -b5- And AlS~aArimu (tropical:) The lion. (K, TA.)

A calamity (K, TA) that extirpates everything. (TA. [See also SuraAmN , last sentence.]) -A2- Also Firm, or sound, of judgment. (K.) -A3- And i. q. wajobapN , (S, M, K,) like SayolamN , (TA,) i. e. An eating once in the day: (M, K, * TA: *) or, accord. to Yaakoob, an eating at the time [ of morning ] called AlD~uHaY (M, TA) [ and not again ] to the like time of the morrow: (TA:) one says, fulaAnN yaA^okulu AlS~ayorama (S, M, * K *) i. e. [ Such a one eats ] once (K, TA) in the day: but AHát says, I asked El-Asma'ee respecting the bazomap and the Sayoram , and he said, I know it not: this is the language of the devil. (TA.)

A man having the extremity of his ear cut off. (Mgh.) ― -b2- See also muSorimN . ― -b3- Also [the fem.] SaromaA='u A she-camel having little milk; (M, K;) because her abundance of milk has become cut off: (M:) pl. SuromN . (K.) See also SuraAmN . [In the Ham, p. 230, it is implied that it signifies A she-camel such as is termed ↓ as meaning whose A^axolaAf (or teats ) have been cut off: for it is there said that the poet 'Orweh has applied the term SaromaA=' to (assumed tropical:) a cooking-pot, likening it to the she-camel termed muSar~amapN meaning as expl. above.] ― -b4-

Also, (S, K,) or falaApN SaromaA='u , (M,) A desert in which is no water. (S, M, K. [See also one of the explanations of the dual, here following.]) ― -b5- AlA^aSoramaAni signifies The wolf and the crow; (ISk, S, M, K;) because of their separating themselves (ISk, S, M) from mankind: (ISk, S:) and the [ bird called ] Surad and the crow: and the night and the day; (K, TA;) because each is cut off from the other. (TA.) El-Marrár says, EalaY SaromaA='a fiyhaA A^aSoramaAhaA waxir~iytu AlfalaApi bihaA maliylu [ Upon a waterless desert, in which are its wolf and crow, and in which the skilful guide of the desert is burned by the sun ]. (ISk, S, M.) And tarakotuhu biwaHo$i AlA^aSoramayoni is a saying mentioned by Lh, but not expl. by him: (M, TA:) ISd says, (TA,) in my opinion it means, [ I left
A narrow place, that quickly flows with water: (K, TA:) so called because the flow of water is quickly cut off from it. (TA.)

A possessor of a Siromap of camels. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence], as also ↓ , (M, K,) Having little property: (M:) or poor, [ and ] having a numerous household, or family. (K.) One says, kalaA^N tiyjaEu minohu kabidu AlmuSorimi [ Herbage by reason of which the liver of him who has little property is pained ]; i. e., abundant, so that when he who has little property sees it, he grieves that he has not many camels which he may pasture upon it. (M.)
The curved knife of the parer of spindles. (S, MA, K.)

A she-camel whose [ fore or kind ] pair of teats have been cut off, (S, M, K,) in order that the A_iHoliyl [or orifice through which the milk passes forth from the udder of each teat] may dry up and the milk not issue, for the purpose of giving greater strength to her: and (AA used to say, S) this is sometimes in consequence of the stoppage of the milk, something having happened to the udder, for which it is cauterized, and her milk stops, (S, K,) no milk ever issuing from the udder: (S:) see also SaromaA='u , voce A^aSoramu : or muSar~amapu AlA^aTobaA='i means a she-camel treated ( Euwlijato ) so that her milk has stopped. (Mgh.)
: see SariymN , first and second sentences.

senses.text: 1 , (S, M, Msb,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. SarFY , (M, Msb,) said of water, It remained, or stagnated, long: or it remained long, and became altered [ for the worse ]: (S, Msb:) or, said of water and of milk, it remained so that its flavour became altered [ for the worse ]: (M:) or, said of milk, it remained undrawn from the udder, so that its flavour became bad, or corrupt. (TA.) And SariYa Ald~amoEu The tears collected [ in the eye ] and did not run. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Sariyati Aln~aAqapu , (Fr, M, Msb, TA,) aor. as above, (Msb,) and so the inf. n.; (M, Msb, TA;) but Ibn-Buzurj says Sarat , aor. ; (TA;) The she-camel's milk became collected in her udder; (M, Msb, TA;) as also ↓ . (M, TA.) ― -b3- And SariYa fiY yadihi , (S, M, IKtt, TA,) with kesr; (S, TA;) or SaraY fiY yadihi ;) (thus acc

Also, i. e. SaraAhu , (M, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. SaroYN , (M,) i. q. qaTaEahu [ He cut it off, cut it short, or stopped it; &c.]; (M, K;) namely, a thing. (M.) You say, SaraY bawolahu , inf. n. as above, meaning qaTaEahu [ He, or it, cut short, or stopped, his urine ]. (S.) And Sarayotu AlmaA='a [app. I cut short, or stopped, the drawing of the water; for it is expl. as said] A_i*aA A@sotaqayota vum~a qaTaEota . (S.) And maA yaSoriyka min~iY A^aYo EabodiY , occurring in a trad., means What cuts short ( yaqoTaEu ) thine asking of Me [ O my servant ]? (TA.) ― -b2- And i. q. dafaEahu [ He repelled it ]. (M, K.) One says, SaraY A@ll~`hu Eanohu $ar~ahu i. e. dafaEa [ God repelled, or may God repel, from him his, or its, evil, or mischief ]. (S.) ― -b3- And i. q. manaEahu [ He prevented it, &c.

; or became, or remained, or lagged, behind; syn. taA^ax~ara . (IAar, K.) [Accord. to the TK, one says SaraY Eanohumo , meaning He receded, or retreated, from them; &c.]. ― -b3- Also He, or it, was, or became, high; syn. EalaA . (IAar, K.) ― -b4- And the contr., i. e. He, or it, was, or became, low; syn. safula . (IAar, K.)
2 see 1, former half, in two places.

4 see 1, former half, in two places. ― -b2- ASrY also signifies He sold a ewe or she-goat, (K, TA,) or a she-camel, (TA,) whose milk had been caused to collect in her udder in consequence of her not having been milked for some days; such as is termed muSar~aApN . (K, TA.)
8 i. q. AizodaraAhu [the d in each being substituted for t ]: see the latter, in art. zrY .

, (S, M, Msb, K,) an inf. n. used as an epithet, (Msb,) and ↓ , (S, M, K,) [and Freytag adds ↓ , as from the K, in which I do not find it,] Water remaining, or stagnating, long, accord. to Fr; (S;) or that has remained, or stagnated, long: (Msb:) or water remaining long, (K,) or that has remained long, and become altered [ for the worse ], (S, M, Msb,) accord. to AA. (S.) And the first, (M, K,) an inf. n. used as an epithet, (TA,) Milk that has remained (M, K) long (K) so that its flavour has become altered [ for the worse ]; (M, K;) as also ↓ , which is in like manner applied to water: (M:) or milk left [ long ] in the udder of the camel, not drawn, so that it becomes salt and windy: (IAar, TA:) or milk drawn in the night from a camel abounding therewith, having a bad and burning flavour.
: see SarFY , first sentence: ― -b2- and see also muSar~aApN .

: see SarFY , first sentence. ― -b2- In relation to a she-camel it is Her being pregnant twelve months, and bringing forth, and then yielding her biestings, or having her biestings milked: mentioned by Az. (TA. [But what is meant by this is, to me, doubtful; for sometimes an inf. n., and sometimes and epithet, and sometimes a subst., is expl. in this manner.])
[part. n. of SariYa ]: see SarFY . ― -b2- Also A she-camel whose milk has collected in her udder. (Msb.) [See also muSar~aApN .]
Milk collected [ in the udder ]: a poet says, wakul~u *iY SaroyapK laA bud~a maHoluwbu [ And whatever udder has milk must be milked ]. (TA.)
: see muSar~aApN .

, applied to a man and to a beast, Whose maA=' [i. e. sperma ] has collected in his back. (TA.) -A2- Also The [ bird called ] yamaAmap [n. un. of yamaAmN , q. v.]: and the [ bird called ] samaAmap [n. un. of samaAmN , q. v.]. (TA.)

Colocynths (S, M, K, in the CK [erroneously] SirA'N [expressly said in the TA to be with fet-h and medd,]) when they become yellow; (S, M;) as also SaraAyaAtN : (so in one of my copies of the S [in which it is shown to be correct by an ex. in a verse of Suleyk there cited: in the M and TA SaraAyaA , which I think a mistranscription]: in the other of my copies of the S omitted:) one thereof is termed ↓ . (S, M, K. *) [In the M and K, SaraA='N is termed pl. of SaraAyapN ; but it is properly speaking a coll. gen. n., originally SaraAYN .] ― -b2- ↓ also signifies The water in which colocynths have been steeped. (M, K.)
One who acts with boldness towards the wife of his father: (K, TA:) such was Ibn-Mukbil. (TA.)
: see SaraA='N , in two places.
: see muSar~aApN , below.

[act. part. n. of SaraY : as such signifying] Guarding or preserving [&c.], or a guarder or preserver [&c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] A sailor: (S, M, K:) because he guards, or preserves, the ship: (TA:) pl. Sur~aA='N (S, M, K) and (M, K) pl. pl. (M) SaraAriY~u and SaraAriy~uwna . (M, K. [But see SaraAriY~N in art. (TA.) ― -b3- SaqaEa biDaroTapK , said of an ass, He emitted a sounding wind from the anus, in a moist and dispersed state. (Az, O, TA.) ― -b5- And SaqaEa , (S, O, K,) said of a man, (K,) He went away, (S, O, K, TA,) fiY kul~i Aln~awaA
; or becoming lost; and perishing

; or dying. (TA. [But I think that this is probably a mistranscription for SaqaEN , inf. n. of SaqiEa .]) You say also, SaqiEa fulaAnN naHowa ka*aA Such a one repaired towards such a thing. (TA.) ― -b6- And SaqiEati Albiy^oru , aor. , (A'Obeyd, S,) inf. n. SaqaEN , The well collapsed

; or broke down. (A'Obeyd, S, K. *) -A3- SaqiEato , (TA,) inf. n. SaqaEN , (O, K, TA,) said of horses, and of birds, &c., They became white (O, K, TA) in the [ SawoqaEap , or] uppermost part of the head, (TA,) or in the middle of the head. (O, K.) ― -b2- And [the inf. n.] SaqaEN , in relation to the head, signifies The being bald: or, as some say, the going away of the hair. (TA.) -A4- SuqiEati AlA^aroDu The earth, or ground, became overspread with the SaqiyE [i. e. hoarfrost, or rime ]; (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ ; each with damm. (IDrd, K.)
2 , inf. n. taSoqiyEN , He swore to him respecting a thing: (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K:) and so bq~E lh , inf. n. taboqiyEN . (Ibn-'Abbád, O.)

4 He (a man, O, TA) entered upon [ a time, or a tract, of ] SaqiyE [i. e. hoar-frost, or rime ]. (IDrd, O, K, TA.) -A2- And ASqE AlS~aqiyEu AlA^aroDa , (K, TA,) and Al$~ajara , (O, TA,) The SqyE [or hoar-frost ] fell, or lighted, upon the earth, or ground, (K, * TA,) and the trees. (O, TA.) And A^uSoqiEati AlA^aroDu : see 1, last sentence. And A^uSoqiEa Aln~aAsu The men, or people, became overspread with the SaqiyE . (TA.)
1 : see 1, first sentence. ― -b2- SawoqaEa Alv~ariydapa He spread evenly the vrydp [or mess of crumbled bread moistened with broth ]. (TA.)

A district, quarter, or tract, syn. naAHiyapN , (S, O, Msb, K,) of a country: (Msb:) and a place, region, quarter, tract, or point, towards which a person, or thing, goes, tends, or is directed; syn. jihapN : and a place of alighting, or of descending and stopping or sojourning or abiding or lodging or settling

; or a place of abode or settlement; syn. maHal~apN : (Msb:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aSoqaAEN , (O, TA,) and pl. pl. A^aSaAqiEu : (TA:) and SuqogN is a dial. var. thereof. (IJ, TA; and K in art. Sqg .) One says, fulaAnN mino A^aholi h`*aA AlS~uqoEi i. e. mino h`*ihi Aln~aAHiyapi [ Such a one is of the people of this district, &c.]. (S, O.) And huwa fiY SuqoEi baniY fulaAnK He is in the naAHiyap [or district, &c.], and the maHal~ap [or place of alighting, &c.], of the sons of such a one. (Msb.) See also miSoqaEN . ― -b2- Also A part, or portion, of the surrounding and inferior sides of a well: pl. A^aSoqaAEN : but the more approved word is with s . (TA.)

inf. n. of SaqiEa . (S, &c.) ― -b2- Also An affection like gam~N , [i. e.] that takes away the breath, ( yaA^oxu*u biAln~afasi , S, O, K, [in the CK, bAln~afosi ,]) by reason of the vehemence of the heat. (S, O, K.)

[ Smitten by a thunderbolt: (see its verb, SaqiEa :) or] smitten as by a thunderbolt from the enemy: so accord. to some: (O, TA:) 'Ows Ibn-Hajar says, A^abaA dulayojapa mano liHaY~K muforadK SaqiEK mina AlA^aEodaA='i fiY $aw~aAli (S, * O, TA, but in the TA A^aAabaA ) [which may be rendered O Aboo-Duleyjeh, who is for a solitary tribe, smitten as though by a thunderbolt from the enemies, in Showwál (which was, in the time of the poet, a cold month) ?]: or, accord. to IAar, the meaning here is, in a state of retirement, remote from the enemies; (S, * O;) for when the winter pressed severely upon the man, he used to retire to a distance, lest a guest should alight at his abode; the enemies being the strange guests; and by saying fY $w~Al , he means that the cold was in Showwál: (O, TA:) or Sa
Intenseness of cold; from AlS~aqiyEu [meaning “ hoar-frost, ” or “ rime ”]. (TA.)
A whiteness in the middle of the head of a horse and of a bird &c.; (S, O, K;) or in the middle of the head of a black sheep or goat, accord. to Abu-l-Wázi'. (TA.)
Stupid, dull, or wanting in intelligence: but this is a vulgar word. (TA.)

The first increase, or offspring, ( nitaAj ,) [ of sheep, or goats, ] when the sun smites ( taSoqaEu ) the heads of the lambs or kids: (Aboo-Nasr, O, K: [in the CK, Albuhomi is erroneously put for Albahomi :]) and some of the Arabs call it the $amosiY~ , and the qayoZiY~ : then is the SafariY~ , after the SaqaEiY~ : (Aboo-Nasr, TA:) it is also expl. as signifying such as is brought forth in the [ period called ] Safariy~ap : (TA: [but see SafariY~N :]) and, (O, K,) accord. to AZ, (O,) the young camel that is brought forth in [ the time of ] the SaqiyE [i. e. hoar-frost, or rime ]; which is of the best of the increase [of camels]. (O, K.)

A piece of rag with which a woman protects her ximaAr [or muffler ] from the oil [ in her hair ], (S, O, K, TA,) putting it on her head; (TA;) as also ↓ : (K:) or this latter signifies a thing by which the head is protected, such as a turban and a ximaAr and a ridaA=' . (TA.) ― -b2- And The [ woman's face-veil termed ] buroquE (S, O, K) is sometimes thus called. (S, O.) ― -b3- And A thing with which a she-camel's nose is bound, (S, O, K, TA,) as expl. in art. drj [voce durojapN ], (S,) when they desire her to affect her young one or the young one of another: or, accord. to A'Obeyd, a piece of rag with which her eyes are bound; that with which her nose is bound, [or stopped, (see

1 in art. ZA^r )] when she is made to affect a young one not her own, being termed gimaAmapN . (TA. [But see durojapN .]) ― -b4- And A mark made with a hot iron upon the qa*aAl [or back of the head ] of a camel. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ― -b5- And An iron thing that is in the place of [ the kind of curb called ] the Hakamap of the bit. (O, K.) ― -b6- And A thing that is next to the head of the horse, beneath ( duwna ) the larger buroquE . (TA.) ― -b7- The SiqaAE of a tent ( xibaA=' ) is A rope that is extended from its top, and pulled tight, the two ends of which are tied to two pegs, or stakes, stuck into the ground, when the wind is violent and it is feared that the tent may be thrown down. (O, TA.)

The jaliyd [i. e. hoar-frost, or rime, ] that nips, or blasts, (lit. burns, [see A^aHoraqa ,]) the plants, or herbage; (Msb;) what falls from the sky in the night, resembling snow. (S, O, K.) -A2- Also A species of zunobuwr [or hornet ]: (O, K:) so says AHát, as having been heard by him from a man of Et-Táïf. (O.)
[ Deviating from the truth; as is indicated in the TA: and hence,] a liar: (TA:) one says, Saho SaAqiEu i. e. Be silent, O liar. (Yoo, O, K.)
i. q. SaAEiqapN [i. e. A thunderbolt ]: (Fr, S, O, K:) of the dial. of Temeem: pl. SawaAqiEu . (TA.) [See also SaAEiqapN .]

The place of the whiteness termed SuqoEap in the head of a horse and of a bird &c.: (S:) or the middle of the head [in an absolute sense]: (O, K:) or the top, or uppermost part, [ of the head, or] of the [ cap called ] kum~ap , and of the turban. (O, K, TA: all in art. SfE . [See

1 in that art., where this last meaning is assigned to SawofaEapN .]) ― -b2- And A turban [itself]: (O, K:) and any other thing that protects the head: (TA;) accord. to IDrd, a piece of rag which a woman puts upon her head as a protection. (O. See SiqaAEN , first sentence.) ― -b3- A piece of rag which is tied upon the top of the [ kind of women's camel-vehicle called ] huwodaj , and which the wind blows about. (TA.) ― -b4- The head [or top ] of the [woman's face-veil called] buroquE . (IAar, TA in this art. and voce $ibaAmN [q. v.].) ― -b5- The hollow ( waqobap ) [ that is made in the upper part of a dish] of variyd [or crumbled bread moistened with broth]: (S, O, K, TA:) or the top, or upper part, of variyd . (TA.) ― -b6- Also The place of a battle in which is much smiting. (IDrd, O, K.)

, applied to a horse, and a bird, &c., Having a whiteness in the middle of the head: (S, O, K:) or a horse white in the top of his head: (Mgh:) fem. SaqoEaA='u , (S, O, K,) applied to an eagle ( EuqaAb ), (S, O, TA,) and to a female ostrich [&c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- AlA^aSoqaEu A certain bird, resembling the EuSofuwr [or sparrow ], in the feathers and head of which is a whiteness, found near water; mentioned [in the K] in art. sqE [as with s in the place of S ]: (TA:) accord. to Ktr, (O, TA,) the bird called AlS~ufaAriyapu [q. v.]: (O, K, TA:) you may form its pl. after the manner of substs. [i. e. saying A^aSaAqiEu ], because it is an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates

; or after the manner of the epithet [i. e. saying SuqoEN ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Accord. to AHát, AlS~aqoEaA='u signifies A [ bird such as is termed ] dux~alap [q. v.], of a dingy colour, small, with a yellow head, short in the zimik~aY [or tail ] and the legs and the neck: (TA:) or, accord. to him, the SaqoEaA=' with a yellowness is a dux~alap of a dingy yellow colour, small, short in the zimik~aY and the legs and the neck: and all dux~al are with the Arabs of the [birds termed] EaSaAfiyr and Hum~ar : but the SaqoEaA=' with a blackness is a dux~alap of a dingy reddish colour, black in the head, and short in the zimik~aY and the neck. (O.) ― -b4- AlA^aSoqaEu also signifies The forelock of a horse: or the white forelock thereof. (TA.) ― -b5- And AlS~aqoEaA='u , The sun. (S, O, K.)
A place towards which one tends, repairs, or betakes himself. (TA.)
: see SaqiEN , last sentence.

An eloquent speaker or orator or preacher: (S, O, K:) or one loud in voice: (K:) or one who is not impeded in his speech, and who does not reiterate in speech by reason of inability to say what he would, or is not unable to find words to express what he would say: (Katádeh, O, K:) or one who is skilful, and penetrating, or effective, in his speech: (O:) or one who goes into every ↓ , i. e. naAHiyap , [meaning province, ] of speech: (TA in this art. and in art. rqE :) [said to be] from AlS~aqoEu meaning “ the raising of the voice; ” (O, TA; *) or from AlS~uqoEu [expl. above]
; or, as some say, from SaqaEahu meaning “ he struck him upon his SawoqaEap ; ” but this last derivation is far-fetched: (TA:) pl. maSaAqiEu . (O, TA.)
: see SaqiEN , last sentence.
