senses.text: 1 , (S, M, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (M, Msb,) inf. n. SaqolN (S, M, O, Msb) and SiqaAlN , (S, O, Msb,) or the latter is a simple subst., (M, K,) He polished it: (S, M, O, Msb, K;) i. e. a thing, (M,) or a sword, (S, O, Msb,) and the like: (Msb:) and so saqalahu . (S.) ― -b2- Saqala Aln~aAqapa (assumed tropical:) He (a man, AA, O) made the she-camel lean, or light of flesh: (AA, O, K:) and in like manner it is said of journeying: (AA, O:) and in like manner also, Alfarasa the horse: (Sh, TA:) or this means he tended the horse well, with the coverings for protection from cold, and with fodder, and took good care of him. (TA. [See SiqaAlN , below.]) ― -b3- Saqalahu biAlEaSaA (tropical:) He struck him, or beat him, with the staff, or stick, (Z, O, K, TA,) and disciplined him. (Z, TA.) ― -b4- And Saq

, (so in a copy of the M,) or ↓ (K,) [the former, if correct, perhaps a contraction, by poetic license, of SaqilN , for which it is not a mistranscription, as is shown by a verse cited as an ex. of it in the M,] Light, or active; applied to a beast ( daAb~ap ). (M, K.)

The xaASirap [or flank ]; as also ↓ : (S, M, O, K: [in the CK, erroneously, Saqolap :]) the former, in this sense, said by AA to be from Saqala Aln~aAqapa : (TA:) seldom is the Suqolap of a horse long except his sides be short, which is a fault: (S, O:) and the SuqolaAni are the qurobaAni [by which may be meant either the two flanks or the two portions between the groin and the armpit on each side ] of a daAb~ap [i. e. horse or similar beast] &c. (M.) And The janob [or side ]. (M, K.) HumurN zaHaAlifu AlS~uqoli means Asses having smooth and fat bellies. (Ibn-'Abbád, TA in art. zHlf .) ― -b2- And i. q. naAHiyapN [meaning A district, quarter, tract, &c]: (O, TA:) so in the saying, A^anota fiY SuqolK xaAlK [ Thou art in a vacant district &c.]; like SuqoEK xaAlK . (TA.) -A2- See also SaqolN .
Length of the flanks; in a horse: (S, O:) or depression ( AinohiDaAm ) of the flank. (M.)

A horse long in the flanks: (S, O:) or long in the flanks and short in the sides: (AO, TA: [see SuqolN :]) and (O) having little flesh, (O, K, TA,) whether long or short, (O, K,) or whether long in the flank or short. (TA.) ― -b2-
Also, applied to a man, (Ibn-'Abbád, O,) Differing, or varying, in his gait
; or manner of walking. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.)
: see SuqolN . ― -b2- Also Leanness, or lankness in the belly, and slenderness. (TA.)

an inf. n. of Saqalahu , (S, O, Msb,) or a simple subst. (M, K.) [See 1, first sentence.] ― -b2- SiqaAlu Alfarasi (assumed tropical:) The tending of the horse well, taking good care of him, supplying him with fodder and fattening him. (S, * M, O, * K.) One says, Alfarasu fiY SiqaAlihi [ The horse is in his state of good tending and feeding ]. (S, O.) [See also 1, second sentence]. -A2- Also The belly. (K.)
A thing, (M,) or a sword, (Msb,) [and the like,] Polished; as also ↓ . (M, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And A thing, such as iron, and copper, smooth, solid, and impenetrable to water. (Msb.) ― -b3- [
Also, as a subst., implying the meaning of an epithet,] A sword. (S, TA.)
: see SayoqalN .
Polishing: pl. SaqalapN . (S, M, Msb, K.)

One who practises the art of polishing (S, M, O, Msb, K) and sharpening (M, K) swords (S, M, O, Msb, K) and the like: (Msb:) [commonly called in the present day ↓ :] pl. SayaAqilapN (S, M, O, Msb, K) and SayaAqiylu : (so in a copy of the M:) the p in the former pl. is affixed irregularly, as in malaAy^ikapN and qa$aAEimapN . (M.)
: see the next paragraph. -A2-
Also, applied to a speaker, an orator, or a preacher, i. q. miSolaqN , (M, K,) used by a poet in the sense of the latter word, i. e. as meaning Eloquent. (Th, M.)

(S, M, O, K, KL) and ↓ (KL) An instrument, (S, M, O, KL,) or a xarazap [which may here mean either a bead-shaped stone or a shell ], (K,) with which one polishes (S, M, O, K, KL) a sword (S, O, KL, TA) and the like, (S, TA,) a knife, (KL,) a mirror, a garment, or piece of cloth, and paper. (TA.)

: see SaqiylN . ― -b2- maSoquwlu AlkisaA='i means (assumed tropical:) Milk overspread with a pellicle: (O, * TA:) a rájiz says, fahowa A_i*aA maA A@hotaAfa A^awo tahay~afaA yuboqiY Ald~uwaAyaAti A_i*aA tara$~afaA Eano kul~i maSoquwli AlkisaA='i qado SafaA [ And he, when he thirsts, or experiences the hot south-west wind ( Alhayof ), leaves only the pellicles when he sucks in with his lips from every quantity of milk overspread with a pellicle, that has become clear ]: accord. to As, it means the froth of milk: (TA:) IAar explained it accord. to its apparent signification, as used in a verse of 'Amr Ibn-ElAhtam El-Minkaree, (O, TA,) i. e. as meaning a [glossy] red kisaA=' ; [a sense not indicated by that verse, and clearly inconsistent with the ex. cited above;] and when told how As had exp

senses.text: 1 , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. Sak~N , (Mgh, * Msb, TA,) He struck him, or it: (S, Mgh, O:) or he struck him, or it, vehemently, with a broad thing

; or in a general sense, (K, TA,) with anything whatever: (TA:) or he slapped him with his hand, i. e. struck him with his expanded hand, (Msb,) like laTamahu , (TA in art. lTv , &c.,) upon the back of his neck, and upon his face. (Msb.)

Hence, in the Kur [li. 29], faSak~ato wajohahaA (S, TA) And she slapped her face with her hand; syn. laTamatohu . (Jel.) And Sak~a AlbaAziY Sayodahu The hawk, or falcon, struck his prey with his foot, and so cast it down. (Ham p.

799.) And [hence, app.,] one says, xu*o h`*aA A^aw~ala Sak~K , meaning A^aw~ala maA A^aSuk~u bihi [ Take thou this on my first striking with it ]: and so A^aw~ala SawokK (O, TA.) ― -b2- Also He pushed him, or thrust him; (As, TA;) like dak~ahu and lak~ahu . (TA in art. dk .) ― -b3- And Sak~a AlbaAba He shut, or closed the door: (S, O, Msb, K:) or he locked the door. (Lth, O, K.) -A2- And Sak~a , aor. and inf. n. as above, He wrote what is termed a Sak~ [expl. below]. (Msb.) -A3- Sakikota , (S, O, K,) like malilota , (K,) third pers. Sakka , (MA, in which it is mentioned as said of an ass,) [and it is also implied in the TA that the third pers. is Sakika , like laHiHato said of the eye, and some other instances, which are extr.,] a verb of the class of taEiba , (Msb,) inf. n. SakakN , (S, M
3 [ He struck him, or it
; or struck him, or it, vehemently, with a broad thing, or with anything
; or slapped him with his hand; being struck, &c., by him ]. (Ham p.

8 They (two men, O, TA, and two bodies, TA) struck each other. (O, TA.) One says, taSoTak~u rukobataAhu [ His two knees collide, or knock together ]. (S, O, Msb. *) And AiSoTak~uwA biAls~uyuwfi They struck one another with the swords. (TA.)

inf. n. of Sak~a . (Mgh, * Msb, TA.) -A2- Also a Pers. word (S, O) arabicized, (S, Mgh, O, TA,) A certain writing, (S, O, K, *) called in Pers. jak , (O,) or Jako ; (TA;) a debenture, or written acknowledgement of a debt (Mgh, Msb) of money or property, or of some other thing: (Mgh:) and a written statement of a commercial transaction, purchase or sale, transfer, bargain, contract, or the like: (Msb, TA:) i. q. sijil~N [in this last sense or in the senses next following]: (S and TA in art. sjl :) a sijil~ of a qaADiY [i. e. a sealed, or signed and sealed, statement of a judicial decision; a judicial record

; or the record of a judge, in which his sentence is written ]: (KL:) and a written order for the payment of subsistence-money, or of a stipend, salary, pension, or allowance; which some persons used to sell, but the selling of which is forbidden: (Msb, TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aSuk~N and [of mult.] SikaAkN and SukuwkN . (S, O, Msb, K.) [Hence,] layolapu AlS~ak~i The night of the middle [ of the month ] of Shaa- bán; because in it are written the SikaAk of the allowances of subsistence [of individuals]: also called layolapu AlbaraA='api . (O, TA.) [Hence also] Sak~u AlmusaAfiri The traveller's pass, given him to prevent any one's offering opposition to him. (A and Mgh in art. jwz .)

The vehemence of the midday-heat in summer: (K:) or the most vehement heat of midday in summer: (S:) and it is prefixed to EumaY~ : (K:) one says, laqiyutuh Sak~apa EumaY~K , (S, O,) a prov., meaning I met him in the most vehement heat of midday in summer when the heat almost blinded by its vehemence: (Lh, O, TA:) for EumaY~ is said to be an abbreviated dim. of A^aEomaY : (S, O, TA:) and by it is said to be meant the gazelle, because he is dazzled and confounded in the midday-heats of summer, and knocks against the thing that is before him: some say, Sak~apa HumaY~K , from Hamiyati Al$~amosu : and some assert that EumaY~ means the heat, itself: (O, TA:) or it is the name of a certain man [as will be found expl. in art. EmY , with variations of this saying]. (S, O, K, TA.)
The air [or atmosphere, between heaven and earth ]; like sukaAkN ; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K;) a dial. var. of the latter word. (Ibn-'Abbád, O.)
Weak: (IAmb, Hr, K, TA:) of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; [lit.] meaning one who is struck much, or often, because deemed weak. (TA.)
[ A writer of the statements termed SikaAk , pl. of Sak~N : or, accord. to Golius, as on the authority of Meyd, an actuary, who commits to writing the sentences of the judge ].

Knock-kneed: (S, O, Msb:) or having a colliding ( AiDoTiraAb ) of the knees, and [when used in relation to an ostrich or a horse or the like] of the EuroquwbaAni [which evidently means here, as in many other instances, the hocks ]; as also ↓ ; (K;) which latter [in this sense is rare, and is written in the CK maSak~N , but] is with kesr to the m : (TA:) thus applied to a man; (S, O, K, TA;) and to other than man; (TA;) [i. e.] applied also to a horse; (O;) and to an ostrich, because he is long in step, long-legged, and sometimes, or often, his rukobataAni [here improperly used as meaning “ hocks ”] being near together, his legs strike each other: (S, O:) and a man is also said to be A^aSak~u Alr~ijolayoni : (TA:) the fem. is Sak~aA='u : (Mgh, Msb:) and the pl. is Suk~N . (TA.) ― -b2- Also

Strong: (S, O, K;) applied to a man; and to other than man; (K;) [i. e.] applied to a camel, and to an ass, (S, O,) as in a verse cited in the last paragraph of art. shr ; (O;) and ↓ signifies the same: (K:) the fem. of the former is with p ; (S, O, TA;) which is held by Sb to be rare; for epithets of the measures mifoEalN and mifoEaAlN seldom have p affixed to denote the fem. (TA.) ― -b2- One says also raA^osN miSak~N lilr~uw^uwsi [app. meaning A head strong to butt, or knock, against other heads ]. (K in art. rA^s .) ― -b3- See also A^aSak~u . -A2- Also A lock; syn. migolaAqN . (K.)
: see what follows.
and ↓ are epithets applied to a camel, [app. as meaning Fleshy; ] as though flesh were thrust ( Suk~a , i. e. $uk~a ,) into him. (O.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, K,) [aor. ,] inf. n. SakomN , (TA,) He (a man, Fr, S) struck him, or it. (Fr, S, K.) See also SawaAkimu . ― -b2- And He (a man, Fr, As, S) pushed, thrust, or repelled, him, or it. (Fr, As, S, K.) ― -b3- And one says of a horse, yaSokumu , (S,) or Sakama EalaY lijaAmihi , (K,) or EalaY faA^osi All~ijaAmi , (TA,) The horse champs, (S,) or champed, (K,) his bit, (S, K,) or the fA^s of the bit, (TA,) and stretches forth his head, (S,) or then stretched forth his head, as though desiring to contend for superiority [ with his rider ]. (K.)
A vehement shock, collision, impetus, push, or thrust, (Lth, S, K, TA,) with a stone or some other thing. (Lth, TA.)
i. q. A^axofaAfN [which means Camels' feet, and boots; probably, here, the former: in the TK it is expl. as meaning the hoofs of camels: and it is there said that the sing. is SaAkimN ]. (K.)

[Accord. to the S and K, the verb is app. said of the jabiyn : accord. to the TA, of a man.]) -A2- Salatahu , (S,) aor. , (TK,) inf. n. SalotN , (K,) He urged him to run, by striking him with his foot, or leg

; or struck him with his feet or legs, to urge him; namely, a horse; syn. rakaDahu . (S, K. *) ― -b2- And He poured it forth; namely, what was in the cup, or bowl. (S.) -A3- jaA='a bilabanK yaSolitu , and bimaraqK yaSolitu , He brought milk, and broth, having much water, (T, S, M,) with little oily, or greasy matter. (T, S.)
3 signifies The taking to oneself a verse of another poet without altering anything in it. (Har p.
267. [But this I believe to be postclassical.])
4 He drew his sword from the scabbard. (S, M, A.)

(TA.) One says of the eagle ( AlEuqaAb ), AnoSalatato munoqaD~apF [ It was swift in making a stoop ]. (A. [This meaning is there indicated by the context.]) ― -b2- AnSlt yaEoduw He hastened in some measure, running: and so Ainokadara yaEoduw . , applied to the jabiyn [or side of the forehead], Conspicuous, or clear, or fair; syn. waADiHN : (S, A, K:) open, or uncovered, and even: (M, K:) or smooth: (TA:) anything bare; and open, or uncovered: (IAar, TA.) wide, even, and beautiful, or comely. (IAar, TA.) And rajulN Salotu Alwajohi waAlxad~i A man conspicuous, or clear, or fair, in respect of the face and of the cheek. (TA.) And fulaAnN yukaw~inu AlA^asowada SalotFA [ Such a one makes the black to be white, or fair ]. (TA.) ― -b2-

SuluwHN (S, MA, Mgh, Msb, K * [in the CK AlS~aluwH is erroneously put for AlS~uluwH ]) and SalaAHN (S, * MA, Mgh, Msb, K *) and maSolaHapN ; (MA;) and SaluHa , aor. , (S, MA, Mgh, Msb, K,) mentioned by Fr, on the authority of his companions, (S, TA,) but said by IDrd to be not well established, (TA,) inf. n. ; or he reconciled himself with him: for] muSaAlaHapN is the contr. of muxaASamapN . (Mgh.) And SAlHhu EalaY ka*aA He made peace, or reconciliation, [or a compromise, ] with him on the condition of such a thing. (MA.) And SAlHhu EalaY baEoDi maA lahu [ He compounded with him for part of what was owed to him; he made a compromise with him on the condition of receiving part of what was due to him ]; said of a creditor and debtor. (Mgh in art. DgT .) And SaAlaHotu bayona Alqawomi , inf. n. muSaAlaHapN , I made peace, or a reconciliation, between the people, or party; syn. laA='amotu . (Msb in art. lA^m . [See also

4 , (A, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_iSolaAHN , (S, A,) and quasi-inf. n. SalaAHN , (L in art. lqH ,) said of a man, (A, Msb,) and of God, (TA,) [and of a thing,] He, and it, made, or rendered, it, or him, good, incorrupt, right, just, righteous, virtuous, or honest; constituted it, disposed it, arranged it, or qualified it, well, rightly, or properly; rectified, corrected, redressed, or reformed, it; put it into a good, incorrupt, sound, right, or proper, state

; or restored it to such a state; put it to rights, or in a state of order; set it right, set it in order, ordered it, managed it well, cultured it; adjusted, dressed, or trimmed, it; prepared it properly for use; repaired, mended, amended, or improved, it; made it, or him, to thrive; contr. of A^afosadahu . (S, * K. [And so by implication in the Mgh &c.]) One says, A^aSolaHotu Alqidora biAlt~aAbali [ I made good, qualified properly, or seasoned, ( the contents of ) the cooking-pot with the seeds that are used in cooking ]. (Msb in art. tbl .) And A^aSolaHotu Als~iqaA='a biAlr~ub~i [ I seasoned the skin with rob, or inspissated juice ]. (S in art. rb .) And A^aSolaHotu bayona Alqawomi [in which AlA^amora is understood, so that the meaning is I rectified, or reformed, or amended, the circum

; or] I made peace, or I effected a rectification of affairs, an agreement, a harmony, a reconciliation, an accomodation, or an adjustment; [or I adjusted the affair; ] between the people, or party. (Msb.) And saEaY fiY A_iSolAaHi *aAti Albayoni [ He laboured in rectifying, or improving, the bad, or the good, state of circumstances, or the disunion or union, subsisting between people ]. (A.) One says also, ASlH Ald~aAb~apa , (TA,) and ASlH A_ilaY Ald~aAb~api , (T, A, Mgh, TA,) the latter because ASlH implies the meaning of A^aHosana , (Mgh,) (tropical:) He acted well to the beast, (T, A, TA,) and put it into a good, or right, or proper, state, or took care of it, or paid frequent attention to it. (A, TA.) And ASlH A_ilayohi (tropical:) He acted well to him, did good to him, or benefited hi

(Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] SaliEati AlEurofuTapu , inf. n. as above, (tropical:) The ErfTp [a species of mimosa] dropped the heads of its branches: and had them eaten by the camels. (MF, TA.) And one says of a calamity ( $id~ap ), on the occasion of its befalling, SaAbato biqur~K , meaning It became [or fell ] in its qaraAr [or settled or fixed place, or in the place where it should remain ]. (S, TA. [See also art. q
; or it sloped down; syn. AinoHadara ; and so ↓ . (M, TA. [See also 4, first sentence; and see 2, last sentence.]) ― -b3- [

; or said, or done, right ]. (S, K.) , a post-classical word, A man of the people called the Suwfiy~ap : (Msb:) [formerly applied to any devotee: afterwards, particularly, to a mystic; one who seeks to raise himself to a high degree of spiritual excellence by contemplation of divine things so as to elicit the mysteries thereof: ] the Suwfiy~ap may be so called [from the Greek σοφο͂σ : or] in relation to the people called A=lu SuwfaAn , [see SuwfapN ,] as resembling them in the devotion of themselves to religious exercises: or in relation to those called A^aholu AlS~uf~api , wherefore they are also called AlS~uf~iy~apu : or in relation to AlS~uwf [i. e. wool], which is proper to devotees and recluses: this last is the derivation commonly received. (TA.)
